a.summary: MAIN FIX LOST + DUPLICATE METHOD after hunk 6. v1_tx relocated this overload to the end of the class, so git auto-merged v1_tx's copy while main's edit to it (adding the `requireSignableSignatureLayout()` call from 7377486) sat inside conflict hunk 6. As merged, this overload is the ONLY one of the three that skips the guard — main's block on converting an unsignable parsed signature layout into a mutable Transaction is bypassed by the most commonly used overload (and by every `createTransaction()` / `createTransaction(Instruction[])` / `createTransaction(AccountMeta[])` default that delegates to it). Once hunk 6 re-emits the guarded copy in main's position, this one is also a duplicate-method compile error.

b.summary: MAIN FIX LOST + DUPLICATE METHOD after hunk 6 (test-covered — confirmed by negative control: dropping the guard from this overload makes `mismatchedSignatureLayoutsRemainReadableButCannotBecomeMutableTransactions`, `mismatchedSignatureLayoutWithLookupTablesPreservesCountOrder` and `mismatchedSignatureLayoutWithZeroLookupTablesPreservesCountOrder` fail). v1_tx relocated this overload to the end of the class, so git auto-merged v1_tx's copy while main's edit to it (adding the `requireSignableSignatureLayout()` call from 7377486) sat inside conflict hunk 6. As merged, this overload is the ONLY one of the three that skips the guard — and it is the one every `createTransaction()` / `createTransaction(Instruction[])` / `createTransaction(AccountMeta[])` interface default delegates to. Once hunk 6 re-emits the guarded copy in main's position, this one is also a duplicate-method compile error.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
